## 17.Emerging risk,scenario analysis and stress testing

## 17.1 Emerging risk identification

Emerging risks are newly developing or changing risks whose impact and likelihood cannot yet be reliably quantified. Because they are by definition absent from historical loss data, they will not be surfaced by backward-looking processes and require deliberate horizon scanning.

The Group Risk function performs a quarterly emerging risk scan drawing on regulatory pipelines, supervisory publications, industry bodies, peer loss events, technology developments, macroeconomic and geopolitical analysis, climate science and input from the business. Candidate risks are assessed for velocity as well as potential impact and presented to the Group Executive Risk Committee with a recommended treatment: monitor, investigate, or escalate to the register.

| Cross-borderdatalocalisation requirements | Medium | Helena Vorstermann (EMP-37655) | +44.207555.0163 | Investigate |

## 17.2 Scenario analysis

Scenario analysis assessesexposure to severe but plausible events for which historical data is unavailable or unrepresentative.Scenarios are developed through facilitated workshopswith business,risk andsubject-matter experts,and must explicitly record assumptions made,the control environment assumed,estimated frequency and severity,and therange ofuncertainty aroundthe estimate.

|---|---|---|---|
| Severe cyber intrusion with data exfiltration | Annual | CalebA.Whitfield （EMP-38907) | Tests detection,containment.notification and recovery |
| Failure ofa criticalthirdparty | Annual | DeyanshR,Kulkarni(FMP-39220) | Tests substitutability, exit planning and continuity |
| Prolonged loss ofa core bankingplatform | Annual | Lars-ErikBrannstrom （EMP-41402) | Tests impact tolerance for important business services |
| Large-scale internal fraud | Biennial | Fumiko L.Nakagawa(EMP-38412) | Tests segregation of duties,surveillance and escalation |
| Systemic mis-selling or conduct failure | Biennial | HarrietL.Okafor(EMP-41142) | Tests product governance and redress capability |
| Severe macroeconomic downturn | Annual | Babatunde O.Osei-Tutu (EMP-38550) | FeedsICAAPand credit provisioning |
| Climate transition and physicalrisk | Annual | YevgeniA.Sorokina(EMP-38066) | Assessesfinanced emissions and physical asset risk |

## 17.3Stress testing

Stresstestingquantifiesthe effectofadverse conditionsoncapital, liquidityandearnings.TheGroup conductsregulatory prescribed tests, internal tests alignedto its own profile,andreverse stress tests identifying circumstances underwhichthebusiness model would become unviable.Reverse stresstesting results are reported to theBoard annually and informthe RecoveryPlan.Assumptions andthe sensitivityofresults to them are disclosedalongsideresults; a stress result presented without its assumptionsis not a validreport.

## 17.4 Operational resilience

The Group identifies its important business services,maps the people,processes,technology,facilities,data and third parties on which eachdepends,and sets a Board-approvedimpacttolerance for each.It thentests its ability to remain within those tolerances under severebutplausible disruption.Where testing shows a tolerance cannotbe met,thegap isrecordedas an issue andremediatedunder Section15.

| Trade execution and settlement Client reporting and valuations | 1 hour | Arvind K.Pillai (EMP-41502) | 09/05/2026-passed |

## 17.5 Use of results

calibration, the Recovery Plan, resilience investment and the risk register. The Group Executive Risk Committee reviews the use made Scenario and stress results are not standalone exercises. They must demonstrably inform capital and liquidity planning, appetite of each exercise and reports to the Board Risk Committee where results have not been acted upon.
